name: Macroplastique pivotal trial
question: Does transurethral Macroplastique achieve at least noninferior continence improvement compared with Contigen in women with stress incontinence due primarily to intrinsic sphincter deficiency?

design.population: Adult women with stress urinary incontinence primarily due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency after unsuccessful conservative treatment.

verdictNote: The prespecified Stamey-grade noninferiority margin was met; dryness favored Macroplastique.
takeaway: In women with stress incontinence primarily due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency, transurethral Macroplastique produced more one-grade Stamey improvement and more dryness at 12 months than transurethral Contigen; the prespecified noninferiority criterion was met.

reports.label: Pivotal comparison
reports.citation: Ghoniem G, Corcos J, Comiter C, et al. "Cross-Linked Polydimethylsiloxane Injection for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence: Results of a Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled, Single-Blind Study." *J Urol.* 2009;181(1):204-210. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2008.09.032

results.measure: At least one Stamey-grade improvement at 12 months after last injection; treated-per-protocol risk difference
results.note: Treated-per-protocol analysis in the paper; FDA SSED reports a prespecified 15-percentage-point noninferiority margin met in its all-randomized analysis.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; FDA SSED P040050B PDF pp14–15, Table 6

results.measure: Stamey grade 0 at 12 months after last injection; treated-per-protocol risk difference
results.note: The paper reports a statistically greater dry/cure proportion; FDA SSED calls dryness a key secondary outcome.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Results and Conclusions; FDA SSED P040050B PDF p15, Table 6

results.measure: Mean reduction in one-hour pad weight from baseline at 12 months; mean difference
results.note: Units and values follow the journal abstract.

results.measure: Mean improvement in I-QOL score at 12 months; mean difference

harms.label: Postprocedure catheterization
harms.locator: FDA SSED P040050B PDF p17, Table 7
harms.note: Usually immediate intermittent catheterization in clinic.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.locator: FDA SSED P040050B PDF p17, Table 7

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.locator: FDA SSED P040050B PDF p17, Table 7

delivery.label: Injection technique
delivery.value: Cystoscopic transurethral submucosal injection, typically at three urethral sites, until coaptation; Macroplastique placed 1.5–2 cm distal to the bladder neck.

delivery.label: Repeat injection
delivery.locator: FDA SSED P040050B PDF p13, Table 5; PubMed abstract, Methods
delivery.note: A repeat treatment was permitted after the 3-month visit; FDA treatment table includes one control-assigned patient implanted with Macroplastique.

reports.label: Selected-responder two-year extension
reports.citation: Ghoniem G, Corcos J, Comiter C, et al. "Durability of Urethral Bulking Agent Injection for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence: 2-Year Multicenter Study Results." *J Urol.* 2010;183(4):1444-1449. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2009.12.038
reports.followUp: 24 months after last injection, among 12-month Macroplastique responders
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1445; Results, p 1446

results.measure: At least one-grade Stamey improvement maintained at 24 months among 67 followed 12-month responders (75 eligible)
results.note: Primary followed analysis; no prespecified success threshold or hypothesis test. Eight of 75 responders withdrew.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1445; Figure 3 and Results, p 1446

results.measure: Stamey grade 0 at 24 months among 12-month responders
results.note: Of 38 women dry at 12 months, 33 remained dry; 12 of 29 improved but not dry became dry by 24 months. No prespecified threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Figure 3 and Results, p 1446

results.measure: At least one-grade improvement at 24 months among all 75 selected 12-month responders

values.exp: 56/75 (74.7%) with withdrawals as failures; 64/75 (85.3%) with last observation carried forward

results.note: Sensitivity analyses of attrition; neither is the primary followed analysis.

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in one-hour pad weight from baseline at 24 months in followed responders

values.exp: 53/67 (79.1%); mean 24 g at baseline and 4 g at both 12 and 24 months

results.note: No prespecified threshold; 54/67 (80.6%) had at least 50% reduction at 12 months.

results.measure: Mean change in total I-QOL score from baseline at 24 months among 63 with paired data
results.note: Met the stated 0.05 significance threshold in a two-sided paired t test; no multiple-comparison adjustment.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1446; Results, p 1447

harms.label: Genitourinary adverse events, months 12–24

values.exp: Among 67 followed responders, 4 women had 6 urinary tract infection events during months 12–24; no treatment- or device-related adverse events were reported

harms.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, p 1447
harms.note: Table 2 prints 3.3% for 4 affected women, corresponding mathematically to 122 initially treated; 67 responders were followed.

delivery.label: Retreatment, injection volume, and anesthesia in followed responders
delivery.value: 33/67 (49.3%) received repeat treatment at 3 months; mean first and second treatment volumes were 4.5 and 4.3 mL, mean total volume 6.6 mL per patient; local anesthesia was used for 73% of treatments.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1446
